title: Epic
description: Optional container: one outcome delivered by several Specs. When two teams share it, the Epic context is their only shared glossary.

status.description: Optional: `done` or `cancelled` when a person closes or stops it; draft and active are derived from the children.

owner_team.description: The team accountable for the Epic's outcome. The Epic is multi-team when the Specs under it name two or more `owner_team`s.

context.description: Shared terms and constraints for every Spec under this Epic.

covers.description: The ids of the proposal needs this Epic delivers, when it came from an accepted proposal.

ships.description: How this small goal reaches users, which the product manager picks at planning and a person agrees to with the plan. `incremental` (the default): each Spec is useful by itself and merges to the default branch when it is done. `flagged`: useful only when complete but it can be hidden, so each Spec merges behind a feature flag that stays off, and the `launch` Spec turns it on. `batched`: it must land at once and cannot be hidden, so it gets the goal branch `goal/<id>`, the team integrates each Spec into it (`aidd integrate`), and a person releases it once.

specs.description: The planned Specs, in the order they land, started or not. A goal is ready to release only when each of them is integrated, shipped, or cancelled, so a Spec nobody has started yet still counts. Bookkeeping that re-planning changes: drop a Spec from the list to release the rest without it.

launch.description: For `ships: flagged`: the Spec that turns the feature on for users, planned last. Its Merge approval is the launch, which stays a person's: a standing approval never covers it.
